name: Andy Burnham
role: Labour MP for Leigh (2001–2017) and Makerfield (from 2026), Mayor of Greater Manchester (2017–2026), Prime Minister and Labour leader (from July 2026)
summary: A soft-left Labour and Co-operative politician who calls his approach pragmatic rather than ideological. As Prime Minister he champions English devolution through No. 10 North, public control of water, rail and buses, state-led reindustrialisation, a national care service and proportional representation, alongside fiscal rules, higher defence spending, firm support for NATO and Ukraine, and closer EU ties within red lines that rule out free movement. He wants net migration and the welfare bill down through work and housing rather than cuts.

universal-healthcare.rationale: As Health Secretary he proposed a national care service 'free at the point of use' on NHS principles (2010), and he has defended a public NHS free at the point of use throughout; he calls a single universal system for health and care his goal.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: His 2015 leadership manifesto would end the youth rate of the minimum wage and introduce a living wage for all ages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In his 2026 programme statement he blamed privatisation and a 'failed economic model' that lets wealth be 'extracted and siphoned out', and said thirty years of water privatisation left the system in a poor state; he also calls his government pro-business.

public-ownership.rationale: As Prime Minister he is lifting the bar on public ownership of water, champions public control of rail and buses, and promised 'stronger public control' of energy and water; in 2015 he favoured more public control of rail but not wide-scale renationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In 2015 he said there was 'a case for retaining the 50p top rate' but would not go to 75p; as Prime Minister he has pledged not to raise income tax, VAT or employee national insurance.

unions-good.rationale: At PMQs in October 2026 he said of trade unions, 'I am a proud supporter of them'; he credited the CWU's work at Royal Mail and voted against the 2015 Trade Union Bill.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He wants bill rises banned by cancelling water-company dividends and bonuses, a strengthened water Bill, tougher action against vape shops and adult gaming centres, and in 2015 a ban on zero-hours contracts.

cut-welfare.rationale: He rejects 'crude cuts' such as taking £4 billion from housing benefit and wants to lower the welfare bill through council housing, education and work support, though he also says too many young people are 'stuck on benefits'.

surveillance-ok.rationale: As shadow Home Secretary he supported giving the police and security services investigatory powers 'to do their job in the digital age', called the 'snoopers' charter' label lazy, and backed the Investigatory Powers Bill once safeguards on bulk powers and privacy were added.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: After the 2016 referendum he asked that police and prosecutors 'follow up every single report of hate crime, prosecute wherever possible', citing racist cards and abuse.

state-harmful.rationale: He wants an active state: 'rewiring the British state', a national care service, council housing and public control of essentials, making 'the service of place the state's first priority'.

empower-police-military.rationale: He said in 2016 'I am pro-police' and wanted more police numbers, funding and powers to protect officers; as Prime Minister he backs 3.5% of GDP on defence and 'broken windows' policing, while also pressing for police accountability.

decide-locally.rationale: His 2026 programme promises 'the biggest redistribution of power this country has seen', a devolution deal for every part of England and local models for the home nations, saying 'where power is too centralised and too remote, sometimes poor decisions are made'; but he wants growth driven with 'the full authority of the very centre of Government' through No. 10 North, and devolution to unitary councils and mayors rather than the smallest level.

rehabilitation.rationale: In 2016 he welcomed 'a greater focus on rehabilitation and prisoner education'; as Prime Minister he wants to end indefinite IPP sentences for those who have served their time.

traditional-family.rationale: In 2007 he told the Daily Telegraph 'marriage is best for kids' and that the tax system may recognise marriage; he also backs same-sex marriage, so this is support for marriage rather than a fixed family form.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted for the Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Bill in 2013 and in 2015 publicly urged Pope Francis to back same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted in 2008 against every amendment to lower the abortion time limit.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In 2016 he called for 'an immigration system that affords greater control and reduces the numbers'; as Prime Minister he backs the Home Secretary's reform of indefinite leave to remain and blames the Conservatives for migration 'out of control'.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He says Britain will support the UN so that 'the UN's standing rises in these times, because we need it more now', while being open to UN reform.

nation-first.rationale: He says he stands up for 'the British interest' and will always put Britain first, but argues that control comes through collaboration with European and other partners.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Voted for the 2011 Libya intervention to protect civilians and for the 2003 Iraq motion (which he later said he would not repeat); on Syria in 2013 he backed Labour's amendment requiring a UN process first, and he voted against air strikes in 2015.

open-borders.rationale: He said in 2016 that 'full free movement' was 'not an option' and keeps freedom of movement as a red line as Prime Minister, while wanting greater control of migration.

limit-growth.rationale: He frames climate action as compatible with growth ('growth in every postcode') and says action on climate can bring down the cost of living.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He says he carries 'a clear commitment to a carbon-neutral future', that the government will meet the climate challenge and that the hot summer 'is what the climate crisis looks like'; he rejects the Greens' 'ideological' approach in favour of a managed transition.

land-value-tax.rationale: In 2010 he proposed a land value tax at the heart of tax reform, to replace stamp duty and inheritance tax, not most other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: His 2010 leadership plan would replace inheritance tax with a land value tax; separately he proposed a flat compulsory care levy on all estates in 2010, not heavier taxes on large ones.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He wants to back British industry through public procurement 'before we reach to protectionist measures', and joint action with Europe against cheap Chinese exports.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His 2026 programme calls for 'a more intentional approach to the reindustrialisation of Britain', public control over regional investment strategy and local industrial strategies that identify priority sectors.

direct-votes.rationale: He says referendums divide households and communities and must be approached with great care, and that no referendum is proposed on Europe.

right-to-secede.rationale: He says a Northern Ireland border poll follows the Good Friday agreement when opinion changes and a Scottish referendum would follow majority support, while arguing devolution keeps the UK together.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He repeatedly contrasts 'an ideological approach' with 'a pragmatic approach', saying 'we are not ideological but pragmatic', on energy, Europe and the climate transition.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He supports a two-state solution with Israel and a Palestinian state side by side and condemned an antisemitic motion; he co-operates with Israel on security while opposing settlements.

school-vouchers.rationale: No recorded position on vouchers found in his speeches or interviews.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: As Prime Minister he pledged 'no borrowing to fund day-to-day spending, debt falling as a percentage of GDP' and a government 'grounded in fiscal responsibility'.

national-self-determination.rationale: He defends the Falkland Islanders' 'right to self-determination' and voted in 2014 to recognise the state of Palestine.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: In his 2015 leadership campaign he said freedom to work should not mean freedom to claim and proposed limiting newcomers' access to benefits.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He says 'young people who can work should be working' and wants some support conditional on taking up offered opportunities, after the right help is given first.

class-collaboration.rationale: He describes the Greater Manchester way as public, private, community and trade-union partners pulling together, revives the 'triple-helix' of business, academia and government, and in 2015 promised an industrial strategy made with business and trade unions.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He approved the Jackdaw gas field and says the public would expect Britain to use its own reserves rather than import gas, as a 'bridge to a renewable future'.

proportional-representation.rationale: He says standing under a proportional system 'changed me' and that he is 'in favour of more proportional systems', wanting a mandate at the next election to change the voting system.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He says Westminster is out of touch and 'makes a fraud out of good people', and that politics is 'losing the trust and faith of the public', while praising MPs as good people.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He championed the Hillsborough law, saying it rebalances 'the scales of justice' and ends 'the cover-up culture', and pressed for inquiries into Orgreave; he wants power redressed 'in favour of ordinary people and away from the Executive'.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He advocates a preventative state with public control of essentials, a national care service, council homes and an NHS.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Voted for same-sex marriage and gender recognition and campaigned for gay rights against his own church's teaching.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: He argues the public housing stock is 1.5 million homes smaller than in the 1980s while 1.5 million people wait, and plans the biggest council-house building programme since the war.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voted against the 2015 Trade Union Bill, which tightened ballot and picketing rules, and his 2015 manifesto pledged to oppose it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Wants to loosen the whip system and has criticised suspensions of MPs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He wants a closer relationship with the EU and a long-term dialogue on options, said in 2025 he hoped the UK would rejoin in his lifetime, but keeps the manifesto red lines, including no return of free movement, for this Parliament.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He said in 2015 he would resign from the shadow cabinet if Labour backed leaving NATO, and as Prime Minister says Britain 'will remain at the heart of NATO'.

death-penalty.rationale: Called public executions abhorrent and said he would never support them.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: No position from his own words found; the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia's account of converting climate aid into loans, which is a funding decision rather than a stated view on aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Voted for Trident renewal in 2007 and 2016 and said in 2015 he would quit a shadow cabinet that opposed Trident.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He backs a two-state solution and says settlement building on the West Bank would let it 'die in front of our eyes'.

collective-defense.rationale: He told the House that NATO is a defensive alliance and 'our resolve to defend our allies and ourselves is absolute'.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He calls Russia's war an 'illegal invasion' that Ukraine must be helped to resist and opposes West Bank settlement building.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Voted in 2007 that the remaining hereditary element in the Lords should be removed.

non-intervention.rationale: Voted for the 2011 Libya intervention and as Prime Minister sends air defence and support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He opposed leaving the European Convention on Human Rights in 2016, saying it would dent Britain's moral authority, and pledged to defend the Human Rights Act.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: He opposed compulsory tendering in the NHS ('collaboration over competition') and backs insourcing, but wants employment support delivered through the community, voluntary and social enterprise sector.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Voted for the Gender Recognition Bill in 2004 and earlier backed trans women using women's facilities, but in 2026 said the EHRC single-sex guidance should be implemented while not 'marginalising already marginalised communities'.

assisted-dying.rationale: As Prime Minister he declined to give a stance in July 2026, saying social and palliative care must be fixed first; he was absent from the 2015 Commons vote.

social-market-economy.rationale: He describes 'business-friendly socialism': a pro-business government with sound finances alongside public control of essentials and social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Supports higher defence spending and NATO commitments; says defence of the nation is his first priority.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Supports NATO membership (his 2015 resignation pledge; 'at the heart of NATO' as Prime Minister) and steadfast support for Ukraine.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: In 2015 he urged Pope Francis to bring the Catholic Church 'into the 21st century' on gay rights.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He says he will stick to the Good Friday agreement '100%' and that the priority is getting the Stormont power-sharing executive functioning.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Voted to renew the UK-based Trident system in 2007 and 2016 and threatened to resign over Labour opposing it.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Brought Greater Manchester's buses under public control, says every city should control its public transport, and as Prime Minister is lifting the bar on public ownership of water.

second-chamber.rationale: He wants the unelected Lords replaced, with indirect election as a first stage, and voted for a wholly elected second chamber in 2007 and the 2012 Lords Reform Bill.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Voted for the 2003 Iraq motion (later saying he would not again) and the 2011 Libya intervention.

free-public-college.rationale: His 2015 manifesto would replace tuition fees with a graduate tax, and he voted against raising the fee cap in 2010.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Voted in 2015 for the motion calling on the government to reverse its cuts to tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He says 'we will stick to the fiscal rules' and voted for the Charter for Budget Responsibility in 2014.

public-service-media.rationale: He told the House 'I am a very big supporter of the World Service, and indeed of the BBC as a whole.'

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Voted for Trident renewal in 2007 and 2016 and said in 2015 he would resign from a Corbyn cabinet over its stance on Trident.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He says the Falklands 'are British and will remain so, because that is the overwhelming will of the Falkland Islanders', who 'chose to remain British not so long ago'.

close-ties-china.rationale: He says Britain should keep dialogue open with China, but wants common cause with Europe against 'the damaging effect that Chinese exports are having on our industries' and works chiefly with the US and Europe.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: As Prime Minister he removed VAT from household electricity bills, calling it a tax cut.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He wants care delivered on universal NHS principles, free at the point of use, rather than means-tested.

notes:
Positions shift over time: voted for the Iraq war but later said he would not do so again; earlier supported trans people using facilities matching their gender but backed single-sex rules in 2026; favoured a graduate tax and later tuition-fee abolition. Where a 2026 position as Prime Minister differs from earlier ones, the most recent is used. Many statements are null because no direct evidence was found.
